newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST - HK newspaper editorials - June 24.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - HK newspaper editorials - June 24.

text.p: There are seven days to go before the British colony reverts to China.
These are highlights of comments in the Hong Kong press. The views expressed are those of the newspapers quoted and do not represent an editorial viewpoint of Reuters.

-- HONG KONG ECONOMIC TIMES said the agreement between China and Britain on the transfer of defence was pragmatic, showing Britain's new Labour government had adjusted its China and Hong Kong policy and wanted a cooperative relationship with Beijing. As an era ends with the handover, the Sino-British relationship would become more friendly in the future, the paper said.

-- WEN WEI PO said the agreement on defence showed that the Sino-British relationship was improving. China had always believed cooperation with the British side would benefit itself and Hong Kong. It said the British government should take the handover as a chance to improve its relationship with China and the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, which would be beneficial to Britain's long-term business interests on the mainland and in the territory.

-- APPLE DAILY commented on a recent survey which showed that 70 percent of Hong Kong businesspeople thought freedom of information and expression would be restricted after the handover. It said the media was responsible for safeguarding press freedom. People have to fight for freedom and cannot wait for the rulers to grant it as a charity, it said.
